title: the Hare Krishnas
hook: the name everyone calls them isn't their name. it's a line from their song
tomorrow: can someone not born Hindu belong at the Krishna feast?

segments.voice: The Beatles and the mantra closed with kirtan, where the room answers the voice. Today, the people who took that singing out onto the sidewalk.

Saffron cloth, a drum on a strap, small brass cymbals, and a song with only a few words in it, going round and round on a city sidewalk. Passersby have a name ready: the Hare Krishnas. Here's the odd part. That isn't their name. It's a line from their song, turned into a nickname. Their real name is longer, and it hides a bigger puzzle about who Krishna is.
screen: `SAFFRON, A DRUM, BRASS CYMBALS.` → `A NICKNAME FROM A SONG.` → `WHO IS KRISHNA, FOR THEM?`

segments.voice: The name is the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, ISKCON for short. Krishna consciousness means keeping Krishna in mind, and not only during the singing: while cooking, working, walking to the bus. Devotees point to the Bhagavad Gita. Near its end, Krishna tells Arjuna, in paraphrase: fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer to me, bow to me, and you will come to me. For devotees, that verse is the whole program. Now the puzzle. Other Vaishnavas, devotees of Vishnu, honor Krishna as Vishnu come to earth. This lineage turns that around. Its roots run back to Bengal, to the saint Chaitanya and a family of teachers called the Gaudiya Vaishnavas. For them, Krishna isn't one form of Vishnu among many. He is the Supreme Person himself, the source of everything, Vishnu included. That's worth saying plainly, because Hindus hold it differently. Advaita teachers speak of a reality beyond every name and form. Devotees of Shiva or of the Goddess place them at the center. So the puzzle solves itself: a group named after keeping Krishna in mind, because for them Krishna is the center of everything. The beads, the singing and the kitchens all grow from that one answer.
screen: `ISKCON: KEEP KRISHNA IN MIND.` · `GITA: FIX YOUR MIND ON ME.` · `KRISHNA AS THE SOURCE, NOT ONE FORM.` · `HINDUS HOLD IT DIFFERENTLY.` · then, large: `A WHOLE LIFE UNDER A NICKNAME.`

segments.voice: Pick up something within reach that you'll use later today, a cup, a pen, your keys, and look at it closely. Let one name, or one quiet thought of what you hold dear, rest beside it the whole time you're looking, the way devotees try to keep Krishna in mind through ordinary tasks.
The Hare Krishnas: a nickname from a song, for ISKCON, a Krishna-centered lineage with roots in Bengal.
Something to keep from the Hare Krishnas: a song for a nickname, and a whole life underneath it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Devotees in ISKCON temples chant the Hare Krishna mantra, study the Bhagavad Gita and try to offer their daily work, cooking and worship to Krishna.

chat.says: free lunch on the quad from Hare Krishna devotees. roommate asks: are they Hindu or a whole other religion?
options: Hindu: one Krishna-centered lineage with roots in Bengal, with its own clear answer.
a separate religion that borrowed Hindu songs and left Hinduism behind.
just Hindu, and they believe what every Hindu believes about Krishna.
chat.meaning: ISKCON is a Gaudiya Vaishnava lineage, Hindu, with its own clear answer: Krishna as the source of all. Other Hindus hold it differently.

ISKCON.meaning: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, the movement's own name

Chaitanya.meaning: the Bengal saint whose followers sang Krishna's names

Gaudiya Vaishnavas.meaning: the Krishna-devoted lineage with roots in Bengal

Advaita.meaning: the Vedanta school of one reality beyond name and form

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 18.65 (fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer to me, bow to me, and you will come to me)
